extracted.intended_audience: journalism students, media professionals, and general readers interested in news agencies
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and practical principles that govern how news agencies gather, write, and distribute news (wire services) — including editorial philosophy, story structure, sourcing/attribution, and organizational/distribution models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectivity / avoidance of overt partiality
rubrics_metrics.description: To achieve wide acceptability, the agencies avoid overt partiality. Objectivity (or widely acceptable neutrality) is the philosophical basis for their enterprises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should minimize overt bias so their feed is acceptable to many subscribers; editorial positions and advocacy should be avoided in agency copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy / demonstrably correct information
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrably correct information is their stock in trade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories must be fact-checked and supportable; accuracy is a core evaluative requirement for agency copy intended for redistribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear attribution of sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditionally, they report at a reduced level of responsibility, attributing their information to a spokesman, the press, or other sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use explicit attribution (e.g., 'said a spokesman', 'according to') rather than asserting claims as direct agency fact when relying on third-party statements; attribution helps manage liability and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid making judgments and steer clear of doubt and ambiguity
rubrics_metrics.description: They avoid making judgments and steer clear of doubt and ambiguity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency prose should state verifiable facts and avoid interpretive language, conjecture, or ambiguous framing that implies judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutral editorial style and non-interpretive approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Their reporting generally follows a neutral editorial style and employs a standardized and non-interpretive approach to news writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep tone factual, neutral, and standardized so client newsrooms can reuse copy without editorial adjustment; avoid analysis or advocacy in standard feeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inverted-pyramid structure / emphasize key facts first
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasizing key factual elements at the beginning of news stories, followed by supporting details and background information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with the most important facts (who, what, when, where, why/how), then provide context and background — a standard wire-story structure that facilitates editing and rapid consumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Producing copy usable with little or no modification
rubrics_metrics.description: The major news agencies generally prepare hard news stories and feature articles that can be used by other news organizations with little or no modification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write in a modular, self-contained way (clear datelines, bylines, attribution, concise leads) so downstream outlets can republish directly; avoid localized or client-specific assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of multimedia (images/photos) and specialized production
rubrics_metrics.description: Since the 1960s, agencies delivered specialized production of images and photos, the demand for which is constantly increasing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should supply multimedia assets (photos, wire photos, possibly video) alongside copy, produced to standards that facilitate licensing and reuse by subscribers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution format: bulk electronic delivery via wire services
rubrics_metrics.description: They provide these articles in bulk electronically through wire services (originally telegraphy; today frequently using the Internet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency output should be formatted and packaged for bulk electronic distribution (standardized metadata, datelines, tagging) so subscribers can ingest feeds programmatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational / commercial model affects service and access
rubrics_metrics.description: News agencies can be corporations that sell news or cooperatives that share news centrally; commercial newswire services charge businesses to distribute their news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or choosing a wire service consider whether it is commercial (paid distribution, client services) or cooperative (member-driven sharing) — the model affects pricing, access, and reuse rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial independence considerations for government-funded agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Governments may also control news agencies: China (Xinhua), Russia (TASS), and several other countries have government-funded news agencies which also use information from other agencies as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that state-funded agencies may reflect government perspectives or influence; consumers/subscribers should evaluate potential editorial constraints or propaganda risks when reusing such feeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative agencies emphasize non-corporate viewpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative news agencies provide reporting which emphasizes a self-defined 'non-corporate view' as a contrast to corporate media and government-generated news releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative-wire content may prioritize different story selection and framing; assess fit with audience and accept that such agencies may trade broad acceptability for particular perspectives.
